newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds reverse recent slide on lower CPI data.
newsitem.headline: Bunds reverse recent slide on lower CPI data.

text.p: Bund futures reversed a steady decline from the middle of last week as German inflation reports calmed worries that prices here were climbing.

The March Bund futures contract was up 15 basis points late in the day at 103.36, trading in a narrow range much of the day after the first of four state CPI reports indicated that inflation in February was tame.
In late trade the Federal Statistics Office said that preliminary west German consumer prices grew 1.8 percent in February from a year earlier, slower than 1.9 percent yearly growth in January.
Bunds had been falling steadily since February 18 when the contract hit a high of 104.04, raising fears that the market's technical picture had worsened and that prices could fall.
The tame CPI data overshadowed a strong 2.6 percent increase in January German import prices which at least superfically raised the prospect of "imported inflation."
But analysts said the German economy is too weak for companies to pass on price increases to consumers.
"It is too early to conclude that the Bundesbank's medium-term inflation goal...is in danger," said Lothar Hessler, economist at Trinkaus & Burkhardt.
Traders said that a surprisingly large 8.51 billion mark top up of the Series 121 Bobl probably hurt demand for the issue which did not sell as well as recent issues of the 10-year Bund.

Bunds slipped slightly compared to Treasuries with the spread at 93 basis points, but remained strong against Italian debt despite news the Italian government easily won a confidence vote over its austerity budget.
While domestic factors gave Bunds a lift, traders said the market is mostly concerned with Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony to Congress starting Wednesday.
The long-end of the yield curve outperformed on the day as short maturity issues suffered on speculation that interest rates will not soon be cut.
